text: oh ok cool do i do that on the glass windshield also ?
resolution: User asked whether to also run the new solidify button on the glass windshield. Answered as a how-to clarification — no code changed. Confirmed from the solidifyFaces source that glass is handled specially: the inner-skin copy of a glass face keeps the glass flag (so the pane stays see-through from BOTH sides, fixing the single-sided case where the windshield vanishes when viewed from inside the cab), while the silhouette rim walls are opaque (giving a proper window frame). Told the user they can include the windshield in the same solidify selection as the body faces in one pass — each face type is handled correctly. Flagged the one caveat: thickness is fixed at shellThicknessMeters (0.125m ~5in), which is chunky for glass, and offered to add a thinner/separate glass-thickness option if the framed pane looks too fat. Recommended doing the opaque walls/back-wall/floor first and judging the windshield afterward. Awaiting the user's decision on whether to wire the thinner-glass option.
